claim: createReply makes a reply draft in the existing conversation, which can be edited and sent later. It requires Mail.ReadWrite, so the 'drafts for human review' design on Outlook also needs admin-consent-gated permissions in Microsoft-managed tenants.
excerpt: Create a draft to reply to the sender of a message in either JSON or MIME format....You can update the draft later to add reply content to the body or change other message properties....Send the draft message in a subsequent operation.

title: Microsoft Graph service-specific throttling limits

subject: microsoft
claim: Graph Outlook limits apply per app per mailbox: 10,000 requests per 10 minutes and 4 concurrent requests. Throttling one mailbox does not affect others, which suits multi-tenant scale.
excerpt: The Outlook service applies limits to each app ID and mailbox combination...10,000 API requests in a 10-minute period...Four concurrent requests

title: Exchange Online limits

subject: microsoft
claim: Exchange Online: 10,000 recipients/day per mailbox and 30 messages/minute. The recipient rate limit exists 'to discourage the delivery of unsolicited bulk messages'.
excerpt: Recipient rate limit : To discourage the delivery of unsolicited bulk messages, Exchange Online has recipient limits that prevent users and applications from sending large volumes of email....10,000 recipients per day...30 messages per minute

subject: microsoft
claim: Microsoft says customers needing legitimate bulk commercial email should use third-party specialist providers, and that Exchange Online isn't suited to bulk-mailing scenarios.
excerpt: Exchange Online customers who need to send legitimate bulk commercial email (for example, customer newsletters) should use third-party providers that specialize in these services....Exchange Online isn't suited to accommodate bulk-mailing scenarios.

subject: microsoft
claim: Tenant External Recipient Rate Limit (TERRL): a per-tenant daily cap on external recipients that scales with license count (trial tenants 5,000/day per this page). It is visible to admins in the EAC report. A small customer tenant sending prospecting volume could hit it.
excerpt: Tenant External Recipient Rate Limit (TERRL) : The Tenant External Recipient Rate Limit (TERRL) is the maximum number of external recipients a tenant can send to per day (24-hour sliding window)....This limit depends on the number of licenses a tenant has....The limit for trial tenant is capped at 5,000 external recipients per day.

title: Exchange Online canceling the Mailbox External Recipient Rate Limit (Exchange Team blog)

subject: microsoft
claim: The planned per-mailbox External Recipient Rate Limit (2,000/day) was cancelled indefinitely on 6 Jan 2026. Microsoft says it still aims to stop LOB apps sending bulk email through Exchange Online, by 'smarter, more adaptive approaches', so new controls remain likely. TERRL and the recipient rate limit are unchanged.
excerpt: the Mailbox External Recipient Rate Limit in Exchange Online is being canceled indefinitely at this time ....Prevent misuse of Exchange Online, such as line-of-business (LOB) applications sending bulk email through Exchange Online....The Recipient Rate Limit and the Tenant-level External Recipient Rate Limit mentioned in Exchange Online limits remain unchanged by this announcement.

title: High Volume Email for Microsoft 365

subject: microsoft
claim: Exchange Online High Volume Email (HVE) is for internal recipients only and cannot deliver externally, so it is no route for outreach.
excerpt: Internal recipients within the tenant only...HVE accounts cannot be used for external email delivery.

title: Deprecation of Basic authentication in Exchange Online

subject: microsoft

Search snippets of a 27 Jan 2026 Exchange blog (not verifiable: snapshot unreadable) say default-disable is at end of December 2026 and the final date will be announced in H2 2027.

title: 15 U.S.C. 7704 - Other protections for users of commercial electronic mail (CAN-SPAM), US Code 2023 ed., GovInfo

subject: law-us
claim: CAN-SPAM does not require prior consent for commercial email (opt-out regime), but every commercial email must identify itself as an advertisement or solicitation and carry an opt-out notice and a valid physical postal address. The statute makes no B2B exemption. The FTC guide that says it applies to B2B could not be fetched (ftc.gov blocked the snapshot), so the B2B point rests on the absence of an exemption in the text.
excerpt: (5) Inclusion of identifier, opt-out, and physical address in commercial electronic mail...(A) It is unlawful for any person to initiate the transmission of any commercial electronic mail message to a protected computer unless the message provides—...(i) clear and conspicuous identification that the message is an advertisement or solicitation;...(iii) a valid physical postal address of the sender.

subject: law-us
claim: Opt-out requests must be honoured within 10 business days. This also binds anyone sending on the sender's behalf, so the product needs cross-sequence suppression.
excerpt: for the sender to initiate the transmission to the recipient, more than 10 business days after the receipt of such request, of a commercial electronic mail message that falls within the scope of the request;

title: Electronic mail marketing - ICO Guide to PECR

subject: law-uk
claim: UK PECR: unsolicited marketing email to corporate bodies (companies, LLPs, government) is allowed without consent. Sole traders and some partnerships are treated as individuals and need consent or a soft opt-in. Identity and an opt-out address are always required, and UK GDPR still applies to the personal data (e.g. a named employee's email).
excerpt: You can email or text any corporate body (a company, Scottish partnership, limited liability partnership or government body)....Sole traders and some partnerships are treated as individuals – so you can only email or text them if they have specifically consented...You must not disguise or conceal your identity, and you must provide a valid contact address so they can opt out or unsubscribe.
value: B2B corporate allowed; individuals need consent

subject: law-uk
claim: The soft opt-in covers only existing customers and does not extend to prospects or bought-in lists.
excerpt: The soft opt-in rule means you may be able to email or text your own customers, but it does not apply to prospective customers or new contacts (eg from bought-in lists).

title: Canada's anti-spam legislation (fightspam.gc.ca, Government of Canada)

subject: law-ca
claim: CASL is a consent-based regime: businesses must obtain consent before sending commercial electronic messages, which include B2B prospecting. This page does not detail the implied-consent exceptions (e.g. conspicuously published business addresses); that needs the statute or CRTC guidance (CRTC page unreachable).
excerpt: CASL focuses on commercial electronic messages, which are those that encourage participation in a commercial activity whether or not there is an expectation of profit....by requesting amongst other things, that businesses obtain consent before sending commercial electronic messages.

title: Government notifies DPDP Rules to empower citizens and protect privacy (PIB, MeitY)

subject: law-in
claim: India notified the DPDP Rules on 14 Nov 2025, operationalising the DPDP Act 2023 with an 18-month phased compliance timeline. By inference most obligations bite around May 2027. Data Fiduciaries must give standalone, purpose-specific consent notices.
excerpt: The Government of India has notified the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules, 2025, marking the full operationalisation of the DPDP Act, 2023....The DPDP Rules provide an 18-month phased compliance timeline , allowing organisations time for smooth transition. They also require Data Fiduciaries to issue standalone, clear and simple consent notices

subject: law-in
claim: Data Fiduciaries must promptly notify affected individuals of personal data breaches. As an India-based processor of customer mailbox data, the product inherits breach-notification duties (as fiduciary or processor depending on the contract).
excerpt: In the event of a personal data breach, Data Fiduciaries must promptly inform affected individuals in plain language, explaining the nature and possible consequences of the breach

risk: [ws1 interpretation] Any server-side feature that reads Gmail (sync, reply detection, thread-to-deal linking, AI drafting from content, even header-only gmail.metadata or draft-only gmail.compose) needs a restricted scope. That means restricted verification (several weeks to months), an annual third-party CASA assessment and LOA, and a demo video. Until then the app is capped at 100 users. This is the main launch gate on Google.
mitigation: Budget for CASA from day one; launch a beta inside the 100-user cap; design for least privilege (gmail.readonly + gmail.send rather than full mail.google.com).

risk: [ws1 interpretation] Workspace developer policy bars Gmail scopes for apps that 'distribute spam or unsolicited commercial mail' and approves CRM bulk mail only if 'the user consented to receive emails'. Gmail Program Policies and the AUP ban unsolicited commercial/mass email. Google can revoke API access for the whole app if it enables users to break policy. An automated cold-outreach feature puts every customer's Gmail integration at risk, not just the offending user. Low volume (30-50/day) is no defence, since the policies set no volume threshold.
mitigation: Do not ship automated first-touch sequences to non-consenting recipients over Gmail scopes. Position as correspondence/CRM; if prospecting is needed, get Google's written clarification first or keep it human-composed and sent one at a time.

risk: [ws1 interpretation] The restricted-scope review judges the app's application type from the demo video and justification. A product marketed or demoed as a 'sequencer' or 'cold outreach' tool could be rejected or later revoked, while a CRM / email-productivity framing is explicitly listed as approved.
mitigation: Keep marketing, the consent screen and the demo consistent with the CRM/productivity use case; leave outreach automation out of the verified scope set.

risk: [ws1 interpretation] From May 2026 Gmail API projects have an 80M quota-unit/day threshold above which usage will be billed (pricing not yet published, 90 days' notice promised). Quota increases will need billing. This adds an unknown variable COGS per synced mailbox at scale.
mitigation: Use history.list and push (cheap) rather than polling messages.get; model cost per mailbox once prices are published.

risk: [ws1 interpretation] Workspace admins can block unconfigured apps, set Gmail to Restricted, or specifically block high-risk scopes like sending mail, which disables previously installed untrusted apps. In managed orgs, bottom-up adoption by one rep may be blocked.
mitigation: Provide admin-install docs and a security pack (CASA LOA); target owner-operated Workspace domains first.

risk: [ws1 interpretation] Under the 'Microsoft managed' consent policy (default for new tenants), end users cannot consent to Mail.Read, Mail.ReadBasic or Mail.ReadWrite for a third-party app. Change notifications need Mail.Read and reply drafts need Mail.ReadWrite. Any read/sync/reply-detection/drafting feature on Microsoft 365 therefore needs a tenant admin's consent, while a send-only Mail.Send app stays self-serve. This breaks bottom-up 'connect your mailbox' onboarding for M365 business users.
mitigation: Admin-consent onboarding flow, publisher verification, an admin-facing security pack; target small tenants where the founder is the admin; measure grant rates.

risk: [ws1 interpretation] An unverified multitenant app cannot get user consent where risk-based step-up consent is on. Publisher verification (free, needs a verified Cloud Partner Program account) is effectively mandatory. M365 Certification is optional but 'in some cases' required by tenants.
mitigation: Complete CPP enrolment and publisher verification before beta; plan M365 Certification once enterprise deals require it.

risk: [ws1 interpretation] Microsoft says Exchange Online is not for bulk mail and recipient limits exist to discourage unsolicited bulk messages. It cancelled the 2,000/day mailbox external limit in Jan 2026 but restated its aim to stop LOB apps bulk-sending through EXO via 'adaptive' controls, with TERRL still in force. Automated outreach through Graph sendMail is exposed to future undocumented throttling.
mitigation: Keep sends 1:1 and user-initiated or user-scheduled; do not market EXO as an outreach channel; monitor Exchange Team announcements.

risk: [ws1 interpretation] Gmail sender rules apply per primary domain and to all senders to personal Gmail: SPF/DKIM, spam rate below 0.1% and never 0.3%, rejection enforcement since Nov 2025. Cold outreach from a customer's main business domain puts that domain's reputation, and the rep's own day-to-day mail, at risk; Workspace limit breaches block sending for 24h. 'Unsolicited' is judged by recipients.
mitigation: Product-level send caps far below provider limits, reply/bounce auto-stop, suppression lists, and a warning when sending to non-contacts.

risk: [ws1 interpretation] Legal position on B2B cold email differs by country. US CAN-SPAM is opt-out but requires an ad identification, an opt-out and a postal address, with a 10-business-day honour period. UK PECR allows corporate subscribers but not sole traders/partnerships without consent. Canada CASL requires consent. The EU position could not be verified (EUR-Lex blocked). Automated outreach therefore needs per-jurisdiction compliance features (unsubscribe, suppression, identification), and the customer bears the legal liability.
mitigation: Ship opt-out/suppression for any commercial send; exclude Canada and EU from outreach features until legal review.

risk: [ws1 interpretation] Gmail Limited Use forbids training shared AI models on customer mail (only per-user personalised models) and bars staff from reading mail without explicit per-message consent. The policy also asks for prompt-injection protection. These constrain AI quality loops, support and debugging, and add CASA scope.
mitigation: Inference-only LLM use with zero-retention subprocessors; consent-gated support access; prompt-injection defences; minimal body retention.

risk: [ws1 interpretation] An India-based company processing customer mailbox data comes under DPDP Act 2023 / Rules 2025 (notified 14 Nov 2025, 18-month phase-in to about May 2027): consent notices and breach notification.
mitigation: Map fiduciary vs processor roles in contracts; breach-notification runbook before the phase-in ends.

question: What does a CASA assessment for a Gmail restricted-scope SaaS cost per year, at which assurance level (AL1/AL2), and does the developer pay the lab directly? Google's official pages do not state it; third-party figures conflict ($ hundreds to $75k).
why_it_matters: It sets the fixed annual cost of offering any Gmail read feature, which matters at a small-SaaS price point.
resolve_by: Request quotes from 2-3 CASA-authorised labs listed by the App Defense Alliance.

question: Does Google treat low-volume, individually personalised, user-approved first-touch B2B emails to non-consenting prospects, sent through gmail.send by a CRM, as 'unsolicited commercial mail' that disqualifies Gmail scopes? The policy has no volume threshold and does not define the term.
why_it_matters: It decides whether first-touch outreach can be a feature at all on Google without risking app-wide revocation.
resolve_by: Written clarification from the Google OAuth verification / Trust & Safety team during verification.

question: Are automated follow-ups in an existing thread to a prospect who never replied (the first email having been cold) treated differently from follow-ups to an engaged correspondent? Docs are silent.
why_it_matters: Automatic follow-up is the core wedge; if it inherits the 'unsolicited' label it shrinks to engaged threads only.
resolve_by: Same clarification request; meanwhile auto-follow-up only where the recipient has replied before.

question: What share of target SMB Microsoft 365 tenants run the Microsoft-managed consent policy (admin consent needed for Mail.Read*) versus legacy user consent, and how often do admins grant consent to an unknown sales app?
why_it_matters: It decides whether M365 onboarding can be self-serve or needs an admin-consent sales motion.
resolve_by: exp-permission-test: track consent-flow outcomes for 30+ M365 sign-ups.

question: What will Google charge for Gmail API usage above the 80M units/day threshold, and when does billing start?
why_it_matters: It adds variable COGS per synced mailbox.
resolve_by: Watch the Workspace developer announcements; re-model when prices are published.

question: Under EU ePrivacy Art. 13 and national law, is unsolicited B2B email to legal-person addresses allowed without consent (it varies by member state), and is GDPR legitimate interest available for prospect data? Official EUR-Lex text could not be retrieved in this run.
why_it_matters: EU customers or recipients may make outreach features unlawful in some member states.
resolve_by: Retrieve EUR-Lex texts and national DPA guidance (e.g. CNIL, Datatilsynet) in a follow-up run; get legal advice.

question: What 'smarter, more adaptive' controls will Microsoft use against LOB applications bulk-sending through Exchange Online, and would 1:1 scheduled sequences via Graph be caught?
why_it_matters: Undocumented throttling could silently degrade outreach or follow-up sends.
resolve_by: Monitor the Exchange Team blog; ask Microsoft via partner channel.

question: Does sending Gmail message content to a third-party LLM API, for a user-facing drafting/summary feature, count as a permitted 'transfer to provide user-facing features with user consent' under Limited Use, and what does CASA expect of the LLM subprocessor?
why_it_matters: AI drafting is central to the product; a restrictive reading would force self-hosted models.
resolve_by: Raise during Google verification; document in the demo video and privacy policy.

question: Exact current SMTP AUTH Basic-auth retirement dates in Exchange Online (search leads say default-disable end Dec 2026, final date announced H2 2027; the snapshot was unreadable).
why_it_matters: Relevant only if any design falls back to SMTP; competitors using app passwords lose that route.
